On 31 August 2000, the Ankara Public Prosecutor filed an indictment with the Ankara Criminal Court of First Instance against the applicants and nine others.

The applicants and nine others were charged with having taken part in a demonstration in a public place without the permission of the authorities, contrary to Law no. 2911 on Meetings and Demonstration Marches.
Police officers warned the crowd over a megaphone that the demonstration was illegal under Law no. 2911 on Meetings and Demonstration Marches.

At the material time, section 10 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) required that, in order for a meeting to take place, the governor's office or authorities of the district in which the demonstration was planned must be informed, during opening hours and at least seventy-two hours prior to the meeting, by a notice containing the signature of all the members of the organising board.

Section 22 of Law no. 2911 (the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act) prohibited demonstrations and processions on public streets, in parks, places of worship, and buildings in which public services were based.

Section 22 of Law no. 2911 (the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act) required that demonstrations organised in public squares comply with security instructions and not obstruct individual movement or public transport.

Section 24 of Law no. 2911 (the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act) provided that demonstrations and processions which did not comply with the provisions of that law would be dispersed by force on the order of the governor's office and after the demonstrators had been warned.
Section 16 of Law no. 2559 on the Duties and Powers of the Police provides that the police may use firearms in self-defence.

Section 16 of Law no. 2559 on the Duties and Powers of the Police provides that the police may use firearms if a person or a group resists the police and prevents them from carrying out their duties or if there is an attack against the police.

Additional section 6 of Law no. 2559 on the Duties and Powers of the Police provides that in cases of resistance by persons whose arrest is necessary or by groups whose dispersal is necessary, or of an attack or threat of an attack, the police may use violence to subdue these actions.

Additional section 6 of Law no. 2559 on the Duties and Powers of the Police provides that use of violence refers to the use of bodily force, physical force and all types of weapons specified in the law, and gradually increases according to the nature and level of resistance and attack in such a way as to restore calm.

Additional section 6 of Law no. 2559 on the Duties and Powers of the Police provides that in cases of intervention by group forces, the extent of the use of force and the equipment and instruments to be used shall be determined by the commander of the intervening force.
